name: Main page responsiveness on the representative local archive

description: Baseline cache-busted concurrent main-page API load on the representative archive.

asi.hypothesis: Establish a repeated cache-busted concurrent baseline before changing query ownership or request scheduling.
asi.archive: local archive.sqlite via the running dev server
asi.observations: Work-rhythm is the largest payload and its root execution interval phase is the largest measured server phase; endpoint wall times serialize through the single synchronous connection.
asi.data_guard: Reference JSON captured for harnesses, activity, session shape, usage, and cache-miss responses; work-rhythm excluded by design.

description: Repeat baseline measurement to estimate timing noise; no implementation change.

asi.hypothesis: A second unchanged run would reveal whether the 53 ms baseline was stable enough to use as the comparison.
asi.rollback_reason: No code changed; the lower 42.5 ms result is measurement noise rather than an optimization.
asi.next_action_hint: Use per-phase medians and response sizes to target the root execution interval query and large work-rhythm payload instead of trusting one run.

description: Diagnostic run through the API port with seven samples to separate Vite proxy overhead from server work.

asi.hypothesis: The proxy may be contributing enough variance to obscure query-level wins, so compare the same cache-busted concurrent load directly against port 9000.
asi.rollback_reason: This is not comparable to the page URL baseline and made no code change.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the page-port benchmark as the primary contract, but use Server-Timing and direct probes for query diagnosis; avoid calling timing noise an optimization.

description: Remove the inner root-interval ORDER BY to avoid a temporary sort; timing looked lower but the mutable live archive changed during the run.

asi.hypothesis: Removing the inner JSON aggregation sort should preserve work-rhythm semantics because estimatedWorkIntervals sorts inputs, while eliminating one temporary B-tree.
asi.rollback_reason: The response guard found four non-rhythm mismatches, but the archive changed between the baseline and candidate; this was not a trustworthy code regression. The candidate was reverted pending a stable fixture.
asi.next_action_hint: Freeze a consistent database snapshot or add a database-generation guard, recapture references, then re-test query simplifications.

name: Main page responsiveness on a stable representative archive

description: Stable-snapshot baseline for the concurrent main-page API workload.

asi.hypothesis: Recapture a comparable baseline after freezing the archive snapshot.
asi.observations: The initial request set is dominated by serialized endpoint waits; work-rhythm still spends about 8 ms in root execution interval loading and returns about 209 KB, while non-rhythm response checks are clean.
asi.data_guard: References recreated from the fixed snapshot; work-rhythm remains intentionally exempt from exact equality.

description: Add a covering index for tool execution timestamps used by root work-rhythm interval loading.

asi.hypothesis: A covering index on (model_call_id, completed_at, started_at) should let the root execution interval query satisfy its tool-event join from the index instead of looking up table rows.
asi.observations: The isolated query fell from about 6.2 ms to 3.2 ms with this index; the stable concurrent page median fell from 41.83 ms to 37.23 ms, and the server-reported work-rhythm interval phase fell from 8.2 ms to 4.8 ms.
asi.data_guard: All non-rhythm reference responses matched; work-rhythm payload size and schema remained valid.
asi.simplicity: One migration and one test-fixture migration-list entry; no runtime architecture change.

description: Repeat the covering-index candidate to separate its gain from request-order noise.

asi.hypothesis: Repeating the kept index with no code change will show whether the 11% primary gain survives benchmark noise.
asi.rollback_reason: The repeat was 43.9 ms, above the candidate's 37.2 ms and baseline comparison; response checks passed, so this is timing variance rather than evidence against the index.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the index, use more stable endpoint-level diagnostics, and test a structurally different request-scheduling or work-rhythm split.

description: Add a covering conversation-call index for the subagent usage rollup query.

asi.hypothesis: The usage endpoint's recursive subagent query scans all model calls because it lacks a covering conversation-oriented index; covering its join, date/filter, token, and cost columns should cut that scan.
asi.observations: The isolated subagent query improved from about 3.4 ms to 2.2 ms and the concurrent critical median improved to 35.39 ms from the 41.83 ms stable baseline; usage response latency fell to 13.93 ms. SQLite chose the covering index for the call scan.
asi.data_guard: All guarded non-rhythm responses matched and response byte counts were unchanged.
asi.simplicity: One migration plus the existing test-fixture migration-list entry; the index is write overhead but avoids a runtime query rewrite.

name: Initial dashboard responsiveness with deferred work-rhythm calendar

description: Baseline the split work-rhythm contract with critical summary data and deferred calendar details.

asi.hypothesis: A lightweight summary endpoint can render the work-rhythm overview before the large per-day calendar/timeline payload is fetched, making the initial critical path responsive while retaining all details.
asi.observations: The split benchmark critical median is 32.81 ms with 129.6 KB of critical responses, versus the prior all-data baseline of 35.39 ms and 265.4 KB; summary aggregation fell to about 1.9 ms. The deferred calendar adds about 13 ms to complete data and is 135.8 KB.
asi.comparison_limit: This re-initialized benchmark measures perceived critical readiness, so its primary is not directly comparable to the prior all-concurrent metric; complete time is the comparable tradeoff signal.
asi.data_guard: All guarded non-rhythm responses matched. Work-rhythm summary and days are intentionally exempt because the calendar contract was split.
asi.simplicity: Adds a narrow summary/days contract and one dependent request; no worker pool or general cache.

description: Add a covering index for turn execution timestamps used by root work-rhythm interval loading.

asi.hypothesis: Covering the turn join and execution timestamps should remove table lookups from the root interval query, complementing the kept tool-event covering index.
asi.observations: The isolated query fell from about 3.29 ms to 2.87 ms. In the first split-path run critical_ms was 31.235 and the root execution phase was 4.3 ms; complete_ms also improved versus the split baseline.
asi.data_guard: All guarded non-rhythm responses matched and response sizes were stable.
asi.simplicity: One narrow migration/index; retain only if confirmation shows the small gain is useful.

description: Confirm the turn-execution covering index with seven samples on the stable split workload.

asi.hypothesis: A seven-sample repeat should distinguish the turn index's small isolated query gain from concurrent request-order noise.
asi.observations: The confirmation median was 30.58 ms critical and 42.55 ms complete, below the split baseline of 32.81/46.04; root execution was about 4.1 ms. This supports retaining the index, while endpoint medians remain noisy.
asi.simplicity: No additional code beyond the single index migration.
